p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration showing the process of membrane fusion when neurotransmitters are released from a neuron. The process of membrane fusion when neurotransmitters are released. At the top of the diagram is a neurotransmitter-filled vesicle, which is a circle surrounded by the blue and yellow plasma membrane. The neurotransmitters are pale green dots inside the vesicle; they are labeled to the right. It is labeled “secretory vesicle” on the left. A gray text box to the upper right reads, “Neurotransmitter-filled vesicle approaches plasma membrane.” Below, 2 curved red lines, labeled V-SNARE, bond up to the membrane of the vesicle. Below is the blue and yellow plasma membrane of the neighboring cell. 2 blue curved lines represent proteins labeled t-SNARE curve down and bond to the plasma membrane of the cell. 2 wavy purple proteins, labeled below SNAP25, bond down between the two t-SNAREs. A down arrow points to the vesicle, which is still bonded to V-SNARE. The V-SNARE, T-SNARE, and SNAP25 have braided together to form ropelike chains extending right and left. The cell membrane and the vesicle membrane are now closer together as a result. A gray text box to the right reads, “ v-SNARE and t-SNARE bind to each other, zipping up from the amino termini and drawing the two membranes together.” Below, a down arrow points to the vesicle and membrane beginning to merge; the v-SNARE/t-SNARE/SNAP25 have zipped together even more tightly. They contract vertically as well as horizontally. A gray text box on the right reads, “Zipping causes curvature and lateral tension on bilayers, favoring hemifusion between outer leaflets.” A down arrow points to an almost-fused vesicle and cell membrane. The yellow portions of the membranes are now connected and the protein complex has slightly parted to make room. A gray text box on the right reads, “Hemifusion: outer leaflets of both membranes come into contact.” A down arrow points to the now-fused vesicle and membrane. A pore, shown by a small opening between the two membranes, has now formed. The green neurotransmitters have begun to travel downward through the pore into the cell below. A gray text box to the right reads, “Complete fusion creates a fusion pore.” A final down arrow points to a completely fused vesicle and membrane. The pore has opened wide and the green neurotransmitters spill into the cell rapidly. The protein complexes have pulled apart to release the tension on the membranes. A gray text box to the right reads, “Pore widens; vesicle contents are released outside cell.”
